content: The most reliable method to assess patient adherence to antiretroviral therapy (ART) is by measuring the proportion of individuals enrolled in differentiated service delivery (DSD) ART models who achieve virological suppression. This is defined as having a viral load of less than 1000 copies/mL at six months after ART initiation and at subsequent intervals (e.g., 24, 36, 48, and 60 months). The category other includes transgender and gender-diverse individuals who identify outside the binary classifications of male or female. Syphilis testing coverage measures the percentage of individuals tested for syphilis during a reporting period. This includes: The percentage of individuals attending HIV prevention services who were tested for syphilis. The percentage of people living with HIV who were tested for syphilis during HIV care and treatment services. The percentage of pregnant women tested for syphilis during antenatal care (ANC) services. The rationale for syphilis testing includes: Understanding the burden of syphilis among people living with HIV and populations at elevated risk of HIV acquisition to allocate resources effectively. Testing pregnant women for syphilis is critical for their health and for preventing vertical transmission of syphilis. Knowing testing coverage helps assess the quality of antenatal care services and ensures national screening guidelines are followed. Syphilis testing identifies individuals who would benefit from treatment and measures progress in scaling up screening efforts. Syphilis test positivity measures the percentage of individuals who tested positive for syphilis during the reporting period. This includes: The percentage of individuals attending HIV prevention services who tested positive for syphilis. The percentage of people living with HIV who tested positive for syphilis. The percentage of pregnant women who tested positive for syphilis. The rationale for measuring syphilis test positivity includes: Identifying areas within a country that require additional support and providing early warnings of potential changes in HIV and sexually transmitted infection (STI) transmission. Generating national, regional, and global estimates of syphilis and congenital syphilis incidence and prevalence. Syphilis treatment coverage measures the percentage of individuals who tested positive for syphilis and were treated according to national guidelines during the reporting period. This includes: The percentage of individuals attending HIV prevention services who tested positive for syphilis and received treatment. The percentage of people living with HIV who tested positive for syphilis and received treatment. The percentage of pregnant women who tested positive for syphilis and received treatment. The rationale for syphilis treatment coverage includes: Prompt treatment of syphilis improves individual health and reduces sexual and vertical transmission of the disease. Gonorrhea testing coverage measures the percentage of individuals tested for gonorrhea during the reporting period. This includes: The percentage of individuals attending HIV prevention services who were tested for gonorrhea using molecular tests, culture, or point-of-care (POC) tests. The percentage of people living with HIV who were tested for gonorrhea during HIV care and treatment services. The rationale for gonorrhea testing includes: Gonorrhea is a marker of unprotected sexual intercourse and facilitates HIV transmission and acquisition. Measuring the burden of gonorrhea among people living with HIV and at-risk populations helps allocate resources effectively. Testing for gonorrhea identifies individuals who would benefit from treatment and measures progress in scaling up screening efforts. Gonorrhea test positivity measures the percentage of individuals who tested positive for gonorrhea during the reporting period. This includes: The percentage of individuals attending HIV prevention services who tested positive for gonorrhea. The percentage of people living with HIV who tested positive for gonorrhea. The rationale for measuring gonorrhea test positivity includes: Identifying areas within a country that require additional support and providing early warnings of potential changes in HIV and STI transmission. Generating national, regional, and global estimates of gonorrhea incidence and prevalence. Understanding the challenges posed by increasing resistance to recommended treatment options. Gonorrhea treatment coverage measures the percentage of individuals who tested positive for gonorrhea and were treated according to national guidelines during the reporting period. This includes: The percentage of individuals attending HIV prevention services who tested positive for gonorrhea and received treatment. The percentage of people living with HIV who tested positive for gonorrhea and received treatment. The rationale for gonorrhea treatment coverage includes: Prompt treatment of gonorrhea improves individual health and reduces sexual and vertical transmission. Untreated gonorrhea can lead to pelvic inflammatory disease, ectopic pregnancy, infertility, blindness, and disseminated disease. For all indicators, individual-level data obtained from program records is preferred. If individual-level data is unavailable, aggregate program data can be used, though this may inflate estimates if individuals are tested multiple times during the reporting period.
